verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the command of God our Savior and Christ Jesus our hope,
verses.1:2: to Timothy, beloved son in the faith. Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.1:3: Just as I asked you to remain in Ephesus when I was going into Macedonia, so that you might charge certain people not to teach differently,
verses.1:4: nor pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which produce disputes rather than the edification of God that is in faith.
verses.1:5: Now the goal of the charge is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a faith without pretense.
verses.1:6: Straying from these things, some have turned aside into empty talk,
verses.1:7: wanting to be teachers of the law, understanding neither what they say nor the things about which they make assertions.
verses.1:8: Now we know that the law is good, if anyone uses it lawfully,
verses.1:9: knowing this, that the law is not laid down for a righteous person, but for the unrighteous and insubordinate, the ungodly and sinners, the wicked and defiled, killers of fathers and killers of mothers, murderers,
verses.1:10: fornicators, those who lie with males, kidnappers, liars and perjurers, and anything else that opposes sound teaching,
verses.1:11: which is according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which was entrusted to me.
verses.1:12: I give thanks to Him who strengthened me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because He considered me faithful, placing me in ministry,
verses.1:13: though previously I was a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent man. Yet I obtained the mercy of God, because I acted ignorantly in unbelief.
verses.1:14: And the grace of our Lord overflowed exceedingly, with faith and the love that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.1:15: A trustworthy saying and worthy of complete acceptance: that Christ Jesus came into this world to save sinners, of whom I am the first.
verses.1:16: Yet for this reason I obtained mercy, so that in me first Christ Jesus might show all patience, for the instruction of those who are going to believe in Him for eternal life.
verses.1:17: Now to the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.1:18: This charge I entrust to you, son Timothy, according to the preceding prophecies concerning you, so that in them you may wage good warfare,
verses.1:19: having faith and a good conscience; rejecting this, some have suffered shipwreck regarding the faith,
verses.1:20: among whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I delivered to Satan so that they may learn not to blaspheme.
verses.2:1: I urge, therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, petitions, and thanksgivings be made for all people,
verses.2:2: for kings and all who are in high positions, so that we may live a quiet and tranquil life in all godliness and chastity.
verses.2:3: For this is good and acceptable before God our Savior,
verses.2:4: who wills that all people be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth.
verses.2:5: For there is one God, and also one mediator between God and mankind, the man Christ Jesus,
verses.2:6: who gave Himself as a redemption for all, a testimony in its own times,
verses.2:7: for which I myself was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I speak the truth; I do not lie), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
verses.2:8: Therefore I want the men to pray in every place, lifting up pure hands without anger and dispute.
verses.2:9: Likewise also, women should be in respectable attire, adorning themselves with modesty and sobriety, and not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly clothing,
verses.2:10: but with what is fitting for women, professing godliness through good works.
verses.2:11: Let a woman learn in silence, with all submission.
verses.2:12: But I do not permit a woman to teach, nor to exercise dominion over a man, but to be in silence.
verses.2:13: For Adam was formed first, and then Eve;
verses.2:14: and Adam was not deceived, but the woman, having been deceived, was in transgression.
verses.2:15: Yet she will be saved through the bearing of children, if she remains in faith, love, and sanctification, with sobriety.
verses.3:1: A trustworthy saying: if anyone desires the office of bishop, he desires a good work.
verses.3:2: Therefore a bishop must be irreproachable, the husband of one wife, sober, prudent, respectable, chaste, hospitable, a teacher,
verses.3:3: not given to wine, not violent, but forbearing, not quarrelsome, not greedy, but
verses.3:4: governing his own household well, having children in submission with all chastity.
verses.3:5: But if anyone does not know how to govern his own household, how will he care for the church of God?
verses.3:6: Not a new convert, so that, lifted up into pride, he may not fall into the judgment of the devil.
verses.3:7: Moreover, he must also have a good testimony from those who are outside, so that he may not fall into reproach and into the snare of the devil.
verses.3:8: Deacons likewise must be chaste, not double-tongued, not addicted to much wine, not pursuing shameful gain,
verses.3:9: holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
verses.3:10: And let these also be tested first, and then let them serve, having no charge against them.
verses.3:11: Women likewise must be chaste, not slanderous, sober, faithful in all things.
verses.3:12: Let deacons be husbands of one wife, who govern their own children and their own households well.
verses.3:13: For those who have served well will acquire for themselves a good standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:14: I am writing these things to you, hoping to come to you soon;
verses.3:15: but if I am delayed, so that you may know how you ought to conduct yourself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and support of the truth.
verses.3:16: And manifestly great is the mystery of godliness, which was manifested in the flesh, was justified in the spirit, appeared to angels, was preached to the Gentiles, was believed in the world, was taken up in glory.
verses.4:1: Now the Spirit clearly says that in the last times some will leave the faith, giving attention to spirits of error and to teachings of demons,
verses.4:2: in the hypocrisy of those who speak falsehood and have their own conscience seared,
verses.4:3: who forbid marrying and require abstaining from foods, which God created to be received with thanksgiving by believers and by those who have come to know the truth.
verses.4:4: For every created thing of God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving is to be rejected;
verses.4:5: for it is made holy through the word of God and prayer.
verses.4:6: By setting these things before the brothers, you will be a good minister of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of the faith and of the good teaching that you have followed.
verses.4:7: But avoid silly and old wives' tales; instead, exercise yourself for godliness.
verses.4:8: For physical exercise is useful to a small extent, whereas godliness is useful for all things, having the promise of the life that now is and of the life to come.
verses.4:9: Trustworthy is the saying, and worthy of complete acceptance.
verses.4:10: For to this end we toil and are reviled, because we hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially of believers.
verses.4:11: Command these things and teach them.
verses.4:12: Let no one look down on your youth; instead, be an example for the believers in word, in conduct, in love, in faith, in chastity.
verses.4:13: Until I come, give attention to reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
verses.4:14: Do not neglect the grace that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.
verses.4:15: Meditate on these things; devote yourself to them, so that your progress may be evident to everyone.
verses.4:16: Pay attention to yourself and to the teaching; persist in them. For in doing this, you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.
verses.5:1: Do not reprimand an older man, but appeal to him as a father, young men as brothers,
verses.5:2: elderly women as mothers, young women as sisters, in all chastity.
verses.5:3: Honor widows who are genuinely widows.
verses.5:4: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let her first learn to govern her own household and to make a return in kind to her parents, for this is acceptable before God.
verses.5:5: Now let the one who is genuinely a widow and left alone hope in God and persist in supplications and prayers night and day.
verses.5:6: For she who lives in pleasure is dead while living.
verses.5:7: And command this, so that they may be above reproach.
verses.5:8: Yet if anyone does not care for his own, and especially for his household members, he has disowned the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
verses.5:9: Let a widow be chosen at not less than sixty years old, who has been the wife of one husband,
verses.5:10: having testimony in good works: if she raised children, if she extended hospitality, if she washed the feet of the saints, if she provided for those suffering affliction, if she followed after every good work.
verses.5:11: But avoid younger widows; for when they grow self-indulgent in Christ, they want to marry,
verses.5:12: having condemnation because they have nullified their first faith.
verses.5:13: At the same time, being idle, they also learn to make the rounds of houses; not only idle, but also talkative and meddlesome, speaking what is not proper.
verses.5:14: Therefore I want the younger women to marry, to bear children, to run a household, to give no opportunity to the adversary for reviling.
verses.5:15: For some have already turned back after Satan.
verses.5:16: If any believer has widows, let him provide for them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may have enough for those who are genuinely widows.
verses.5:17: Let the elders who preside well be regarded as worthy of double honor, especially those who toil in word and teaching.
verses.5:18: For Scripture says, "You shall not bind the mouth of an ox that is threshing," and, "The worker is worthy of his pay."
verses.5:19: Do not accept an accusation against an elder unless supported by two or three witnesses.
verses.5:20: As for those who sin, reprove them before everyone, so that the rest may also have fear.
verses.5:21: I solemnly urge you before God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels to observe these things without prejudgment, doing nothing by leaning to one side.
verses.5:22: Do not hastily lay hands on anyone, and do not share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
verses.5:23: Do not keep drinking water, but take a little wine because of your stomach and your frequent weaknesses.
verses.5:24: The sins of some people are evident, going ahead to judgment, while they also follow after others.
verses.5:25: Likewise good deeds are also evident, and those that are otherwise cannot be hidden.
verses.6:1: Let all who are slaves under a yoke consider their own masters worthy of complete honor, so that the name of the Lord and the teaching may not be blasphemed.
verses.6:2: Now those who have believing masters should not look down on them because they are brothers; rather, they should serve all the more, because those who share in the benefit are believers and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.
verses.6:3: If anyone teaches otherwise and does not consent to the wholesome words of our Lord Jesus Christ and to the teaching that is according to godliness,
verses.6:4: he is arrogant, knowing nothing, but ailing over controversies and battles of words, from which spring jealousies, quarrels, slanders, evil suspicions,
verses.6:5: wranglings of people who are corrupted in mind and deprived of the truth, supposing godliness to be gain.
verses.6:6: Godliness with contentment, however, is great gain.
verses.6:7: For we brought nothing into this world, and there is no doubt that we cannot carry anything out either.
verses.6:8: Now having nourishment and covering, let us be content with these.
verses.6:9: For those who want to become rich fall into temptation, and into the snare of the devil, and into many useless and harmful desires that sink people into ruin and perdition.
verses.6:10: For greed is the root of all evils; craving it, some have wandered from the faith and have entangled themselves in many griefs.
verses.6:11: But you, man of God, flee these things; instead, pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, gentleness.
verses.6:12: Contend in the good contest of the faith; take hold of eternal life, in which you were called and confessed the good confession before many witnesses.
verses.6:13: I charge you before God, who makes all things alive, and before Christ Jesus, who rendered testimony under Pontius Pilate, the good confession,
verses.6:14: that you keep the commandment spotless, above reproach, until the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.6:15: which the blessed and only Mighty One will display at His own times, the King of kings and Lord of those who rule,
verses.6:16: who alone has immortality and inhabits inaccessible light, whom no one among mankind has seen, nor indeed can see; to whom be honor and everlasting sovereignty. Amen.
verses.6:17: Command the rich of this age not to be haughty, nor to hope in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God (who supplies us with all things abundantly to enjoy),
verses.6:18: to do good, to become rich in good works, to give readily, to share,
verses.6:19: to store up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of true life.
verses.6:20: Timothy, guard the deposit, avoiding profane novelties of speech and contradictions of falsely named knowledge,
verses.6:21: by professing which, some have fallen away concerning the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.

notes.1:2: Vulgate reads 'dilecto' ('beloved'), whereas the Greek text has 'gnesio' ('true' or 'genuine').
notes.1:4: Vulgate reads 'aedificationem Dei' ('the edification of God'), reflecting a Greek textual variant ('oikodomen') rather than the standard Greek reading 'oikonomian' ('stewardship' or 'administration').
notes.1:13: Clementine Vulgate explicitly includes 'Dei' ('of God') after 'mercy', which is absent from the Greek text.
notes.1:15: Vulgate specifies 'in hunc mundum' ('into this world'), whereas the Greek text reads simply 'into the world'.
notes.1:16: Latin 'ad informationem' conveys instruction, formation, or modeling, rendering Greek 'hypotyposis' ('outline' or 'pattern').
notes.2:2: Vulgate uses 'castitate' ('chastity') here and in 3:4 where the Greek text has 'semnoteti' ('dignity' or 'reverence').
notes.2:8: Vulgate reads 'puras manus' ('pure hands'), whereas the Greek text has 'hosious' ('holy' or 'devout').
notes.2:11: Vulgate renders Greek 'hesychia' ('quietness' or 'stillness') specifically as 'silentium' ('silence') here and in 2:12.
notes.2:15: Clementine Vulgate keeps the singular verb 'permanserit' ('if she remains'), whereas the Greek text shifts to the plural ('if they continue').
notes.3:1: Vulgate repeats the same verb 'desiderat' ('desires') in both clauses, whereas the Greek text uses two different verbs ('aspires to' and 'desires').
notes.3:2: Clementine Vulgate includes 'pudicum' ('chaste') alongside 'ornatum' ('respectable') where the Greek has a single adjective ('kosmion'), and renders Greek 'didaktikon' ('able to teach') with the noun 'doctorem' ('a teacher').
notes.3:11: Latin 'mulieres' can denote either women serving alongside deacons or the wives of deacons.
notes.3:15: Vulgate specifies the second-person singular 'oporteat te' ('how you ought'), whereas the Greek clause is impersonal ('how one ought').
notes.3:16: Vulgate renders Greek 'mysterion' with 'sacramentum' here (in contrast to 'mysterium' in 3:9) and follows it with the neuter relative 'quod' ('which') agreeing with 'sacramentum', rather than the Greek masculine 'hos' ('he who') or the variant 'theos' ('God').
notes.4:3: The Latin syntax is elliptical (zeugma), literally "forbidding to marry, to abstain from foods," with a positive verb such as "requiring" implied before "to abstain." The relative pronoun quod ("which") is neuter singular after plural cibis ("foods"), treating food collectively.
notes.4:7: The Vulgate reads ineptas ("silly" or "foolish"), giving a distinct nuance compared with the Greek bebelous ("profane" or "irreverent").
notes.4:10: The Vulgate reads maledicimur ("we are reviled"), matching the Greek textual variant oneidizometha, whereas many modern editions read agonizometha ("we strive").
notes.4:14: The Vulgate reads gratiam ("grace"), where the Greek text has charismatos ("gift").
notes.5:4: The Vulgate uses the singular verb discat ("let her learn") and regere ("to govern"), referring to the widow herself, whereas the Greek has the plural manthanetosan ... eusebein ("let them [the children or grandchildren] learn to show godliness").
notes.5:5: The Vulgate uses jussive subjunctives (speret ... et instet, "let her hope ... and persist"), whereas the Greek text uses indicative verbs ("has set her hope ... and continues").
notes.5:11: The Vulgate reads luxuriatae fuerint in Christo ("grow self-indulgent/wanton in Christ"), whereas the Greek means "grow wanton against Christ." In the context of 5:9-11, devita ("avoid") means refraining from enrolling younger widows on the church's list.
notes.5:12: Latin primam fidem literally means "first faith" and is widely understood here as an initial pledge or vow of devotion.
notes.5:16: The Vulgate reads the masculine/generic Si quis fidelis ("If any believer"), whereas the critical Greek text has the feminine ei tis piste ("if any believing woman").
notes.6:1: The Vulgate reads nomen Domini ("the name of the Lord"), whereas the Greek text reads "the name of God."
notes.6:7: The Vulgate reads haud dubium quod ("there is no doubt that") and hunc mundum ("this world"), reflecting textual variants where many modern Greek editions omit "it is certain/doubtless" and "this."
notes.6:9: The Vulgate adds diaboli ("of the devil") to "the snare," whereas critical Greek editions read simply "into a snare."
notes.6:10: Latin cupiditas ("greed" or "covetousness") is broader than the Greek philargyria ("love of money"), and inseruerunt se literally means "entangled/involved themselves in" rather than the Greek "pierced themselves."
notes.6:20: The Vulgate reads profanas vocum novitates ("profane novelties of speech"), reflecting the Greek variant kainophonias ("new-fangled speech") rather than kenophonias ("empty chatter").
